title: A Novel Covert Timing Channel for Cloud FPGAs
problem: Cloud FPGA users face covert data exfiltration risk via side-channel attacks that minimize detection by both victims and cloud providers.
motivation: Shared cloud FPGA infrastructure enables adversaries to launch sophisticated side-channel attacks; existing detection mechanisms focus on obvious outgoing traffic.
method: The attack works by controlling the precise timing of AXI protocol handshakes—the standardized signals (valid, ready, backpressure) that coordinate when data moves in FPGAs. These timing variations get encoded into the spacing of network packets leaving the FPGA, secretly embedding data in packet arrival times. The attack produces minimal traffic signatures, making it hard for cloud providers to detect via normal traffic monitoring.
key_novelty: It's the first covert timing channel to exploit AXI protocol handshakes (the data coordination signals in FPGAs) combined with network packet timing in cloud FPGAs.
contributions: AXI-based covert timing channel for cloud FPGA data exfiltration
Bit error rate as low as 0.01988% demonstrating practical viability
Enables remote power analysis attacks on AWS EC2 and similar cloud services
limitations: Focused on demonstration of vulnerability; defense mechanisms or mitigation strategies not proposed.
primary_theme: AXI-based covert timing channel in cloud FPGAs
